title: Maximum Product of Word Lengths
statement: Choose two words from `words` at different positions that have no letter in common, and return the largest value of the first word's length times the second word's length over all such choices. If every pair of words shares at least one letter, return `0`.
constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The brute-force idea is to compare every pair of words letter by letter, which costs O(n² · L) for words of length up to L. The only thing that matters about a word here is **which** letters it uses, and there are just 26 of them. That set fits in one integer: bit `k` is on when the word contains the letter `'a' + k`. Two words share no letter exactly when their bitmasks have no bit in common, so `(maskA & maskB) === 0` answers the question in one step.

## Approach

1. Build `masks`: for each word `i`, OR together `1 << (letter - 'a')` for every character.
2. Set `best = 0`.
3. For every pair `i < j`, if `masks[i] & masks[j]` is `0`, the words are letter-disjoint; update `best` with the product of their lengths.
4. Return `best`, which stays `0` when no pair qualifies.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["abcw","baz","foo","bar","xtfn","abcdef"]`. `"abcw"` sets the bits for a, b, c and w, and `"xtfn"` sets those for x, t, f and n. Their AND is `0`, so `4 · 4 = 16` becomes `best`. The longest word, `"abcdef"`, shares a bit with every other word (`f` with `"foo"` and `"xtfn"`, `a` or `b` with the rest), so it never pairs. The other disjoint pairs, such as `"abcw"` with `"foo"` (12) or `"baz"` with `"xtfn"` (12), are smaller, so the answer is `16`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n² + T), where T is the total number of letters: one pass builds the masks, then each pair costs O(1).
- Space: O(n) for the masks.

## Pitfalls

- Repeated letters set the same bit twice; that is fine with `|`, but adding `1 << k` instead would break the mask.
- Compare `(masks[i] & masks[j]) === 0` with the parentheses: in JavaScript, Java and C, `===` / `==` binds tighter than `&`.
- The two words must be at different positions; starting `j` at `i + 1` guarantees it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `masks[i]` | 26-bit set of the letters in `words[i]` |
| `ch` | the current character while building a mask |
| `best` | largest product found so far |
| `i`, `j` | the two words being compared |

narration.2: One integer per word will record which of the 26 letters it uses.
narration.3: Build the mask for each word in turn.
narration.5: Turn on the bit for this letter; repeated letters just set it again.
narration.9: No disjoint pair has been found yet, so the best product is 0.
narration.10: Pick the first word of the pair.
narration.11: Pair it with every later word, so each pair is checked once.
narration.12: The AND is zero only when the two words have no letter in common.
narration.13: They are disjoint: keep the larger of best and the product of their lengths.
narration.17: Return the largest product, or 0 if no pair qualified.
